channel.title: California Uzbek — Latest
channel.description: Independent analysis · Central Asia & world geopolitics

item.title: Germany recruits Uzbek truck drivers: €1,800 monthly after tax
item.description: Uzbekistan's Migration Agency, with German firm RecruitMed, opened a competition for 50 positions, requiring C and CE licences, with six months of free German-language training and online interviews on 6 and 10 November.

item.title: Nodir Jonuzoq: state-language use in agencies was below 50% seven years ago, now fully in Uzbek
item.description: The head of the state-language development department told the 'Oydin Gurunglar 2026' forum that 5,292 geographical names have been standardised and the Terminology Commission approved nearly 100 terms after a 30-year pause.

item.title: New Imkon centre opens in Samarkand: preschool for 150 children and rehabilitation for 100 a month
item.description: The new centre in the National Agency for Social Protection's network combines education and treatment; the network provided over 546,000 treatments in 2025.

item.title: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visits Karshi State University: 14,000 students, 3 new dormitories, 7 laboratories
item.description: According to the Presidential Press Service, the head of state toured the university's internationally accredited programmes, joint degrees and research laboratories during a trip to Kashkadarya.

item.title: How to verify information: lateral reading, the SIFT method and reverse image search
item.description: Checking a claim before you share it is the foundation of media literacy. This practical reference explains the techniques professional fact-checkers use — lateral reading and the SIFT method, reverse image search, and how to judge whether a source is reliable — on the basis of sources.

item.title: The establishment of Uzbekistan–Turkey relations: the first country to recognise it (1991–1996)
item.description: Turkey was the first country in the world to recognise Uzbekistan’s independence. This historical reference sets out the establishment of diplomatic, educational and economic ties between the two states in 1991–1996, with exact dates and facts.

item.title: The four changed letters of the revised Uzbek alphabet: an Uzbek tradition or a Turkic turn?
item.description: The letters Ş, Ç, Ö, Ğ in the revised Uzbek Latin alphabet look Turkic to many. In fact they were already part of the original 1993 alphabet. The arguments and objections around the reform.

item.title: Ohio: after Haitian migrants lost protection, Springfield began to empty out
item.description: After the Trump administration ended Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haitians, Springfield — home to roughly 15,000 migrants — is seeing workers dwindle and some businesses close.

item.title: The 1944 deportation of the Crimean Tatars to Uzbekistan and the making of a community
item.description: In May 1944 the Soviet government deported the entire Crimean Tatar people from their homeland; most were resettled in Uzbekistan. This historical reference sets out the exact dates, figures, consequences and road to rehabilitation on the basis of sources.

item.title: Uzbekistan to play friendly against Saudi Arabia in Doha on November 17
item.description: According to the Uzbekistan Football Association, Fabio Cannavaro's side will face Saudi Arabia in Doha on November 17; a friendly against Russia is also scheduled for November.

item.title: Uzbekistan's annual inflation eased to 6.4% in September, core inflation at 5.5%
item.description: The Central Bank said inflation fell from 8% a year earlier but warned that price pressures persist, keeping monetary policy tight.

item.title: Ziroat Mirziyoyeva named chair of global network supporting seriously ill children
item.description: The initiative was announced in Samarkand at the Second International Congress on Childhood Cancer; Uzbekistan's First Lady will chair the network for two years and received a WHO certificate of recognition.

item.title: How ETFs and index funds work: the basics of passive investing and diversification
item.description: An index fund or exchange-traded fund (ETF) lets a single purchase buy a slice of dozens or hundreds of companies. This neutral reference explains passive investing, diversification, the expense ratio and the risks, on the basis of sources. It is not financial advice.

item.title: Russia steps up expulsions in Novosibirsk: 32 Uzbek citizens removed on October 16
item.description: Expulsions of foreign nationals from the Novosibirsk region rose about 59% in a year; Uzbek citizens make up a large share of those removed for migration violations.

item.title: Top destinations for Uzbek travelers: Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan and Tajikistan lead
item.description: Nearly 5.9 million Uzbek citizens traveled abroad for tourism in January–September 2026, with most choosing three neighboring countries.

item.title: Law on the revised Uzbek alphabet signed on Uzbek Language Day
item.description: On 21 October — Uzbek Language Day — President Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed a law improving the Latin-based Uzbek alphabet. The revised alphabet will have 28 letters and one apostrophe; four letters will be written differently.

item.title: The exodus of the 1990s: the emigration of Russians, Jews and Germans from Uzbekistan (1989–2000)
item.description: On the eve of independence and in its first years, Uzbekistan's European minorities — Russians, Jews and Germans — left the country en masse. This history reference explains the 1989 census figures, the reasons and destinations of the emigration (Russia, Israel, the US, Germany) and its demographic consequences, on the basis of sources.

item.title: How the Hijri (lunar) calendar works: how months are set and why Ramadan shifts each year
item.description: The Hijri calendar is a lunar calendar of 12 months based on the Moon's motion. This reference explains its structure, why Ramadan and the two Eids move about 11 days earlier each year, how a month begins (crescent sighting vs. calculation), the origin of the Hijri era, and the key religious dates, on the basis of sources.

item.title: Why sexual-harassment cases are hard to track in Kazakhstan
item.description: An incident on an Astana bus again highlighted the legal gap in recording and tracking public sexual harassment in Kazakhstan. With no dedicated criminal provision, such cases are not separated out in the statistics.

item.title: How electoral systems work: majoritarian, proportional and mixed systems, and the referendum
item.description: An electoral system is the set of rules that turns votes into seats. This neutral reference explains majoritarian, proportional and mixed systems, the difference between presidential and parliamentary systems, what a referendum is, and the core principles of a free election, on the basis of sources.

item.title: Uzbekistan joins NATO's "Partnership for Peace" (1994) and its early foreign policy
item.description: On 13 July 1994 Uzbekistan signed NATO's Partnership for Peace Framework Document. This history reference explains what the programme is, Uzbekistan's multi-vector foreign policy in its early years, and the later cooperation milestones, with precise dates drawn from sources.

item.title: Labour flow to Russia falls 13.2% while remittances reach $9.3 billion
item.description: The Central Bank's H1 2026 Labour Market Review: fewer citizens going to Russia, remittances rising, and destinations shifting towards Europe and East Asia.

item.title: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian: 'Muslims should unite rather than split into two camps'
item.description: In an Al Jazeera interview, Iran's president spoke about Muslim unity, his readiness to join a 'Mecca alliance', and regional security.

item.title: Iran says it shot down a US drone over the Strait of Hormuz; the claim is unverified
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on 20 October they intercepted a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz — its claimed 54th US drone. The US did not confirm it; CENTCOM says the strait stays open to trade.

item.title: How bonds work: face value, coupon, yield and risks
item.description: A bond is a security through which a government or company borrows money and repays it with interest. This reference explains the key terms of a bond, the inverse relationship between price and yield, the types of bonds, the risks, and Uzbekistan's steps into the international bond market, on the basis of sources.

item.title: Google Pay officially launches in Uzbekistan
item.description: Google launched Google Pay and Google Wallet in Uzbekistan on 19 October at the C5+1 digital technologies session in Samarkand; the Central Bank is integrating Humo, Uzcard, Visa and Mastercard.

item.title: Uzbekistan signs the Artemis Accords on space exploration
item.description: Uzbekistan joined the US-led Artemis Accords in Samarkand on 19 October, becoming the 77th signatory; the document was signed by Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov.

item.title: Mirziyoyev calls for faster ID-card border crossings with Tajikistan
item.description: On 19 October President Shavkat Mirziyoyev urged speeding up a system that would let citizens cross the Uzbekistan–Tajikistan border with an internal ID card, citing growing trade, freight and close family ties.

item.title: Over 1.3 million citizens received free medicines in nine months
item.description: According to the Ministry of Health, more than 1.3 million citizens received free medicines under the reimbursement program in January–September 2026; the state reimbursed 248.2 billion soums.

item.title: How social-media algorithms and the "filter bubble" work: why your feed shows what it shows
item.description: The feed on Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and X is sorted by an algorithm, not by time. This reference explains how an algorithmic feed works, the concepts of the "filter bubble" and the "echo chamber," what the research evidence actually says, and the European Union's new rules, on the basis of sources.
